MECE 4520 introduces data science and machine learning through real engineering systems.

::: {.course-status}
- Location: TBD
- Time: **Tuesday & Thursday** 10:10am - 11:25am
- Lecturer: Changyao Chen (cc2759@columbia.edu)

Course materials and source files are available on [GitHub](https://github.com/changyaochen/MECE4520).

## Course focus

Rather than treating machine-learning methods as disconnected algorithms, the course follows a practical engineering progression:

> **understand engineering data → build predictive models → diagnose systems → learn representations → make decisions and control systems**

Students will work repeatedly with a small number of real mechanical-engineering datasets, including gas-turbine emissions and CNC milling tool-wear data. This makes it possible to connect model choices to the systems, sensors, variables, and operating conditions that produced the data.

## Grading policy

The course grade is based on:

| Component | Weight |
|:--|--:|
| Homework assignments | 40% |
| In-class quizzes | 20% |
| Final project | 40% |

Students should expect approximately seven homework assignments and regular
in-class quizzes over the semester. The final project will be completed in
groups and presented as a five-minute presentation on a selected
engineering-data topic.

## Syllabus

This syllabus may evolve as the Fall 2026 course is finalized.

| Class dates (2026) | Topic | Main data or system |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Before Sep. 8 | Python, NumPy/Pandas, linear algebra, and probability refresher | Short exercises |
| Sep. 8 — asynchronous<br>Sep. 10 | Course launch, Python/data foundations, engineering EDA, and measurement variability | Gas turbine |
| Sep. 15 & 17 | Simple and multiple linear regression | Gas turbine |
| Sep. 22 & 24 | Statistical inference for regression, prediction intervals, and regularization | Gas turbine |
| Sep. 29 & Oct. 1 | Logistic regression and classification metrics | CNC tool wear |
| Oct. 6 & 8 | Validation, leakage, grouped splits, and temporal train/test splits | Gas turbine + CNC |
| Oct. 13 & 15 | Decision trees, random forests, and gradient boosting | Gas turbine + CNC |
| Oct. 20 & 22 | PCA, dimensionality reduction, and clustering | Gas turbine + CNC |
| Oct. 27 & 29 | Neural networks and nonlinear function approximation | Gas turbine + CNC |
| Nov. 3 — Election Day (no class)<br>Nov. 5 | Sequential data, degradation, and optional signal processing | CNC tool wear |
| Nov. 10 & 12 | Reinforcement-learning foundations: bandits, states, actions, rewards, and MDPs | Mechanical decision examples |
| Nov. 17 & 19 | Bellman equations, dynamic programming, Q-learning, and SARSA | Gridworld + simple physical systems |
| Nov. 24<br>Nov. 26 — Thanksgiving (no class) | Function approximation and deep Q-networks | CartPole + mechanical control |
| Dec. 1 & 3 | Policy gradients, PPO, continuous control, and RL versus classical control | Pendulum + control systems |
| Dec. 8 & 10 | Final project presentations | Student-selected engineering system |

## A note on the prerequisites

Introductory statistics will be taught primarily in the context of modeling
problems rather than as a long standalone sequence.

Reinforcement learning and sequential decision-making will receive expanded coverage,
 including when RL is—and is not—a sensible choice compared with
 classical-control approaches.
